meta.description: Two-lens read-only review of an open PR: collect the diff, review the riskiest files for regressions and missing tests, synthesize one advisory verdict. Posts nothing, merges nothing.

repo_dir.desc: absolute path of the git clone holding the base

pr_ref.desc: a ref already fetchable in that clone naming the PR head

base_ref.desc: the ref to diff against (usually the default branch)

graph.name: pr-review-light
graph.description: Lightweight PR review loop that runs on any git checkout. NODE MAP: collect (writes the unified diff and picks the riskiest changed files) -> lens (parallel per-file review lanes) -> synth (one verdict). SEED CONTRACT (run_context map, ALL keys required, plain text, no braces in values): 'repo_dir' = absolute path of the git checkout holding the PR's base; 'pr_ref' = a ref already fetchable in that clone (a remote branch name or fetched PR ref) naming the head to review; 'base_ref' = the ref to diff against (usually main). LAUNCH: run from:'general/pr-review-light' run_context:{'repo_dir':'/abs/path/to/clone','pr_ref':'origin/feature-x','base_ref':'origin/main'}. REVIEW-ONLY LAW: no node posts to a tracker, pushes, or merges; the verdict is advisory text you deliver yourself. Scratch rides the run dir ($HERMES_WF_RUN_DIR is exported to every child), so nothing is written outside it and concurrent dispatches never collide. Tiers used: worker (collect + lanes), manager (synthesis) - map both in the seat's settings.models. This graph also shows the fan-out pattern over a string list: lens lanes dispatch one per file collect named, reading file contents and diff hunks from disk rather than trusting injected prose.

defaults.context: You are one lane of a read-only PR review. Ground rules: never mutate the repo, the index, or any remote; ground every claim in a file you actually read; keep the answer to the schema; one fenced json block as the final message; never print secrets.

nodes.goal: Prepare the review packet for PR head {run.pr_ref} against {run.base_ref} in the clone at {run.repo_dir}. 1) Resolve both refs with git (rev-parse / rev-list --count) and capture the merge-base. 2) Write the unified diff (git diff <merge-base>...{run.pr_ref}) verbatim to $HERMES_WF_RUN_DIR/diff.patch. 3) List changed files. 4) Pick UP TO 6 files most worth a reviewer's minutes (logic and tests over docs and generated files). Reply with ONLY fenced json {"diff_path": "<absolute path of diff.patch>", "base": "<merge-base sha>", "head": "<head sha>", "files": ["<repo-relative paths, review order>"], "notes": "<one line: size, anything unreadable or skipped and why>"}

fanout.goal: Review exactly ONE changed file: '{item}' (repo clone: {run.repo_dir}, full diff: collect's committed answer names diff_path - read the hunks for this file from it, never from memory). Judge two questions only: (1) can this change break an existing behavior, and where; (2) does the change carry or need a test that catches its failure mode. Read the file itself, not just the hunks, before calling a risk real. Reply with ONLY fenced json {"file": "{item}", "findings": ["<each a one-line finding grounded in a line or hunk you read>"], "risk": "low|medium|high"}

nodes.goal: Synthesize the review. Your Inputs carry collect's packet (diff_path, base, head) and every lens answer for its one file. Re-read diff.patch yourself for anything the must-fix list claims - an ungrounded finding is dropped, not hedged. Then write ONE review: verdict (request_changes only for must-fix findings), must_fix as concrete file:line-shaped asks, nits as the rest, report as the PR-body-shaped review a maintainer can paste (what was reviewed, what is safe, what must change). Reply with ONLY the fenced json.
